patches.value: If D=0, choose x₀∈E by H001. Projection F→I is onto and 1-Lipschitz. Mapping covers by this map cannot increase diameters, so dim_H(I)≤dim_H(F). Since I has nonempty interior in ℝ, the pinned interval dimension theorem gives dim_H(I)=1. Thus dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. For n=0, this branch handles the only possible E⊆ℝ⁰: E is the singleton, D=0, and no replacement of zero-diameter covers by positive-diameter subsets of ℝ⁰ is needed. Combine with the upper bound for n≥1.
Instantiate the theorem with X=ℝⁿ, s=E, and d=s (the NNReal coercion of the positive real exponent used in the lower-bound branch).
Instantiate the theorem with α=[0,1], β=ℕ, μ equal to Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,1], and summand f(i,t)=ρ_i^s·1_{J_i∩[0,1]}(t).
